afteryang.title: After Yang + Verse
afteryang.event: Kogonada and Noam Argov in person; tickets on sale
afteryang.text: Kogonada’s quiet science fiction treats memory, adoptee identity and technological personhood as intimate family questions. The added short and both filmmakers in person make this the week’s most complete event, and it leaves enough time to reach Metrograph for the Hamaguchi introduction.

lantern.title: Raise the Red Lantern / 大红灯笼高高挂
lantern.when: Daily Nov 6–12 · Fri/Sat 12:20, 1:30, 3:00, 4:15, 5:40, 7:00 & 8:20 PM; see daily listing
lantern.text: Zhang turns architecture, ritual and color into a system of confinement, with Gong Li giving one of the defining performances of Fifth Generation cinema. The restoration is the week’s essential canonical big-screen revisit and offers enough showtimes to avoid Saturday’s guest-event cluster.

asako.title: Asako I & II / 寝ても覚めても
asako.event: Introduction by Kogonada; one listed screening; tickets on sale
asako.text: Hamaguchi’s double-casting romance moves from infatuation and projection toward the harder work of living with another person. Kogonada introducing the only listed show turns a familiar masterpiece into a genuine occasion—and it pairs cleanly with his MoMI appearance earlier that afternoon.

lost.title: Lost Highway
lost.when: Fri Nov 6 · 11:00 PM; Sun Nov 8 · 9:20 PM
lost.event: Two listed screenings; tickets on sale
lost.text: Lynch makes identity itself feel like a crime scene, collapsing jealousy, surveillance and wish-fulfillment into nightmare logic. Two late shows are enough to keep it below the guest-bearing Saturday films, but it remains a direct-focus big-screen priority.

yousee.title: You Can See Everything
yousee.event: Extended NYC run; tickets on sale
yousee.text: This remains the clearest match for the preference you articulated: a public controversy routed through performance, consent, manipulation and the unstable border between documentary and fabrication. The citywide extension removes scarcity, but it should not remove focus—book a full 174-minute slot this week if you have not already seen it.

everytime.title: Everytime
everytime.when: Nov 6–12 · 3:30, 6:15 & 8:45 PM daily through Wed; see Thu listing
everytime.event: MUBI GO selection confirmed Nov 6–12; verify eligible theater/showtime in app
everytime.text: Wollner bends grief into a reality-shifting family voyage, capped by an audacious Tenerife passage. MUBI’s live Friday metadata confirms it as the new Film of the Week; the concentrated FLC schedule makes this a good use of the ticket once the app confirms an eligible session.

possible.title: Possible Love / 가능한 사랑
possible.text: Lee’s collision of class, documentary authorship and desire is a direct-focus film, but you already saw it at NYFF and the Nov. 24 35mm pairing with Heartbeat is the meaningful rewatch. Treat these IFC sessions as flexible access, not the scarce ticket.
possible.event: Regular IFC run; Nov 24 35mm + Heartbeat remains the format upgrade

soul.title: Soul Patrol
soul.text: Harper reconstructs the suppressed history of the first Black special-operations team in Vietnam through archives, reenactment and trauma. Sundance’s directing prize and tonight’s Q&A lift the 7:15 screening above the regular run.
soul.event: Q&A with director J.M. Harper; tickets on sale

suzhou.title: Suzhou River / 苏州河
suzhou.when: Fri Nov 6 · 9:10 PM; Sun Nov 8 · 4:00 PM
suzhou.event: Part of Kogonada: A Way of Looking; tickets on sale
suzhou.text: Lou Ye’s first-person camera turns Shanghai’s polluted river into a zone of unreliable memory, doomed romance and stolen images. It is a strong Asian-cinema counterpoint to the weekend’s Kogonada events, though the direct Hamaguchi introduction has higher scarcity.

housemaid.title: The Housemaid / 하녀
housemaid.event: One listed screening; tickets on sale
housemaid.text: Kim’s delirious class and desire machine remains one of Korean cinema’s foundational shocks, and its influence on Bong Joon-ho is easy to feel without reducing it to a precursor. The noon slot creates a real conflict with MoMI; choose it only if you can forgo Testament and still reach After Yang.

twoseasons.title: Two Seasons, Two Strangers + Nagahama
twoseasons.event: Q&A with Sho Miyake, moderated by Christopher Radcliff; tickets on sale
twoseasons.text: Miyake adapts Yoshiharu Tsuge into two seasonal encounters whose apparent simplicity hides a complex meditation on writing and connection. The Q&A is substantial, but it overlaps After Yang; Kogonada is the stronger personal match, so this is the painful conflict to flag.

devils.title: The Devils
devils.when: Nov 6–10 · 8:30 PM nightly at FLC; IFC 35mm Sat Nov 7 · 7:25 PM
devils.event: Final week of the uncensored restoration
devils.text: Russell’s collision of religious power, state violence, desire and spectacle finally survives in the full cut he wanted. The new 35mm print still matters, but the extended run lowers urgency relative to the one-night introductions and Q&As.

gentlecreature.title: A Gentle Creature / Кроткая
gentlecreature.when: Fri Nov 6 · 6:30 PM; Wed Nov 11 · 4:00 PM
gentlecreature.event: Part of first complete North American Loznitsa retrospective; tickets on sale
gentlecreature.text: A returned parcel sends Loznitsa’s nearly silent protagonist through the machinery of a prison town and the deeper absurdity of authoritarian bureaucracy. It is an unusually rigorous retrospective booking, with Friday night the better slot unless the A24 conversation at 7 PM matters more.

paper.title: Paper Tiger
paper.event: Free preview with James Gray; reservations open soon, member priority
paper.text: Gray returns to 1980s Queens and Brooklyn for a classical tragedy of loyalty, family and compromised aspiration. The free preview with Gray is exactly the sort of event likely to disappear quickly; monitor the official page and claim a reservation as soon as MoMI opens it.

life.title: Life and Debt
life.event: 25th anniversary Q&A with Stephanie Black; tickets on sale
life.text: Black’s argument about IMF and World Bank policy remains a model of documentary form serving economic analysis rather than flattening it. The 35mm print and director Q&A make this a better occasion than a routine anniversary screening.

tickled.title: Tickled
tickled.when: Fri Nov 6 · 7:00 PM; Sun Nov 8 · 5:00 PM
tickled.event: 10th-anniversary Q&As with David Farrier and distinct guests; tickets on sale
tickled.text: Farrier’s escalating investigation is a useful precursor to your interest in manipulation, consent and who controls a nonfiction story. Each screening has a different post-film conversation; choose Friday only if you can give up Loznitsa or Soul Patrol, otherwise Sunday is the clean fit.

lea.title: The Craft of Acting: Léa Seydoux
lea.event: Léa Seydoux with author Isaac Butler; consult official page for current availability
lea.text: A live Criterion recording can move past publicity questions into process, influence and performance construction. Seydoux’s range across Denis, Cronenberg, Bonello and contemporary studio cinema makes this the week’s strongest craft conversation.

sans.title: Sans Soleil
sans.event: One listed screening; tickets on sale
sans.text: Marker’s letters and images move through Japan, Guinea-Bissau and the act of remembering itself, making memory feel both documentary evidence and fiction. After your response to Ulysses’ Gaze, its exile-adjacent movement through history and lost images is especially resonant.

clockwork.title: A Clockwork Orange
clockwork.text: Kubrick’s collision of stylized violence, free will and behavioral control remains culturally corrosive and formally imitated. The 35mm presentation is real value, though Friday’s three-way event conflict makes the Loznitsa and Soul Patrol conversations more urgent.

alice.title: Alice Coltrane’s Eternity’s Pillar
alice.event: BAM x Alfreda’s Cinema x ARTNOIR; tickets on sale
alice.text: Coltrane’s self-made devotional television joins music, scripture, meditation and moving image outside conventional film grammar. Its rarity and spiritual-formal ambition make it a valuable alternative to the simultaneous James Gray preview and DOC NYC launch.

hamaguchi.title: All of a Sudden / Soudain
hamaguchi.when: FLC previews Wed Nov 18 · 6:15 PM & Thu Nov 19 · 7:00 PM; MoMA Thu Nov 19 · 6:00 PM
hamaguchi.text: You want a guest-bearing rewatch. FLC now confirms Hamaguchi Q&As on both Nov. 18 and 19; use those before MoMA’s overlapping fallback, and set a Nov. 12 10:30 AM reminder only if you still need the MoMA ticket.
hamaguchi.event: Hamaguchi Q&As at both FLC previews; MoMA conversation Nov 19. MoMA public sale Nov 12, 10:30 AM ET

yangbeach.title: That Day, on the Beach / 海灘的一天
yangbeach.text: Yang’s little-screened debut already contains his career-long attention to women’s time, modernity, memory and the social architecture of Taiwan. Three dates make this the most important newly actionable direct-focus repertory announcement.

bitter.title: Bitter Christmas
bitter.event: Tickets on sale; exact daily times on official listing
bitter.text: An actress writes from other lives inside a film invented by an Almodóvar-like filmmaker. Its layered traffic between experience and fabrication makes it a good match for your new nonfiction-and-authorship interest, even though it is fiction.

cameron.title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
cameron.text: Anderson’s 35mm record of Winter’s sold-out Carnegie Hall performance is a compact A24 occasion with a format-specific reason to go. It belongs in the 30-day window even without a guest announcement.

minotaur.title: Minotaur / Минотавр
minotaur.event: Zvyagintsev Q&As after 3:00 and 6:30; tickets on sale
minotaur.text: Zvyagintsev’s return puts patriarchal and governmental corruption inside a wealthy household. The two director-bearing sessions are the reason to book early; choose 3:00 or 6:30 rather than the non-event screenings.

blackox.title: Black Ox / 黒の牛
blackox.text: Lee Kang-sheng’s dialogue-free performance and Sakamoto’s final score make this a strong adjacent match for Tsai-focused taste. MoMA has confirmed the week but not showtimes; monitor rather than guessing a ticket deadline.

nuisance.title: Nuisance Bear
nuisance.text: By shifting perspective toward the polar bear, the film asks who gets labeled a nuisance when migration meets tourism, policing and colonial land use. Its formal viewpoint and ethics-of-observation thread make it a high-fit new release; IFC has confirmed the opening, not the times.
